clue.text: International organisation college brought in regarding waste

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived 'in the matter of', i.e. regarding

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so the college letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: dross is waste matter, scum or rubbish

explanation.surface: A charity steps in to deal with a college's rubbish problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' looks like the thing being dealt with; it is DROSS, the scum skimmed off molten metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the worldwide humanitarian movement, a body operating across nations.

clue.text: Member of ruling class? Elevated reputation I associated with one

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: note means distinction or repute, as in 'a man of note'
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A posh person's standing rises when allied with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College has supplied many British prime ministers, hence the questioning definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boys of Eton, the elite English school, have long filled government, so one may be called a member of the governing elite.

clue.text: Challenging search has local resident heading off

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word for a local loses its first letter

parts.note: a native is someone born and living in a place

explanation.surface: A tricky police search includes a local who is leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Combative means eager to fight or argue, i.e. confrontational and challenging.

clue.text: Early opera providing sources of operatic recitative for every opera

indicators.note: the source of each word is where it starts, so take the opening letter of each

explanation.surface: A note about an early opera's recitatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo (1607) is among the earliest operas still performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Monteverdi's Orfeo dates from 1607, one of the first works in the genre.

clue.text: Keep overlooking a messy area

indicators.note: overlooking here means neglecting or leaving out the letter named next

parts.note: to stay is to keep or remain

explanation.surface: A castle keep looks down on an untidy patch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' suggests a view from above; it means missing out the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty, short for pigsty, is figuratively any filthy, untidy place.

clue.text: Branch dropped in river? That's a shame

indicators.note: something dropped in lands inside, so the branch goes within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
an arm is a branch, as of a tree or organisation

explanation.surface: Someone sighs at a branch falling into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is a mild exclamation of regret or dismay, like saying what a pity.

clue.text: Place for actor: unhappy male lead in Equus

parts.note: feeling down means unhappy
a stag is a male deer, and a stag party is all-male

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Stage direction for a gloomy man playing the lead in Shaffer's play Equus.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstage is the front of the stage, nearest the audience, where a performer may stand.

clue.text: A Roman god will receive a bit of tribute here

definitions.text: A Roman god will receive a bit of tribute here

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the bit of tribute goes inside

parts.note: a Lar was a Roman household god (plural Lares)

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece; here the first letter

explanation.surface: Offerings to a Roman deity are made at a sacred spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes inside A LAR, after the L. The whole clue also describes the answer: the place where tribute to a god is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the table where offerings are made to a deity.

clue.text: Chap notices about energy in followers of Bacchus

indicators.note: the chap and notices go about, that is around, the energy letter

parts.note: a man is a chap
E is the physics symbol for energy
ads are advertisements, notices

explanation.surface: A man spots adverts about energy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' sits between the two pieces it wraps, so the E lands inside the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the frenzied female devotees of the wine god in Greek and Roman myth.

clue.text: Pitiful character — promise falling short, taking money

indicators.note: a word falling short loses its last letter

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
M is short for money, as in £5m

explanation.surface: A wretch breaks a promise when paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm is a contemptible, weak person, as in 'the worm will turn'.

clue.text: Crafty student producing debugger?

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or crafty
a swatter is one who swats, i.e. studies hard (a variant of swot)

explanation.surface: A cunning student creates software that removes bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debugger' suggests programming; here it is a gadget for killing insects. Fly meaning knowing or crafty is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly swatter rids a room of insects, punningly 'debugging' it.

clue.text: Somehow avoids breaking laws, issuing denials

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come out in a new order
broken laws are scrambled, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: Someone escapes conviction for lawbreaking by flatly denying everything.
explanation.walkthrough: AVOIDS rearranged gives DISAVO; LAWS broken gives WALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a refusal to acknowledge something, a repudiation.

clue.text: Excellent book in mostly expensive binding offering harsh commentary

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: the book letter sits in the rest
the trimmed word binds, that is wraps round, the book letter
mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: rich food or fabric is costly, expensive

explanation.surface: A fine book in a costly cover reviewed with biting criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and cutting in tone, as of a critic's remarks.

clue.text: Excellent to receive love in street

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the love letter goes inside

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: It's great to find love in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a thoroughfare, much the same as a street.

clue.text: Not favouring having sex endlessly around noon

indicators.note: the shortened phrase goes around the noon letter
without its end the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: 'at it' is a euphemism for having sex

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to midday sex.
explanation.walkthrough: AT IT loses its final T to give ATI, which wraps round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means against, opposed to, as a preposition: anti the plan.

clue.text: Flight attendant reads out instructions finally after problem

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the problem word

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be in trouble, a problem

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cabin crew member reads out safety instructions after a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: READS rearranged gives ARDES.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess is a woman serving passengers on an aircraft, an air hostess.

clue.text: Wet and weak, is brought on board if that is desirable initially

indicators.note: is is brought in, placed inside the ship letters

parts.note: on board means within SS, the steamship abbreviation
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone timid joins the crew if it suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword convention of putting letters inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sissified means effeminate or feeble; a wet, in British slang, is a feeble person.

clue.text: Area of London cut lights

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as a tail or wages
to light (on) or alight is to land, so lights means lands

explanation.surface: A London district has its street lighting cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning comes down to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Docklands is the redeveloped former dock district of east London around Canary Wharf.

clue.text: Presumed substantial line appears in E Nesbit novel

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, extra large

indicators.note: the line letter appears inside, so it goes within the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sizeable passage is believed to appear in a book by E. Nesbit, author of The Railway Children.
explanation.walkthrough: E NESBIT rearranged gives TENSIBE, and L goes in before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or professed, what is supposed to be true on the face of it.

clue.text: Producer's question over millions invested in sound being insufficient

definitions.note: Producer's reads as 'producer is', the 's linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: invested means put into, so these letters go inside
insufficient means falling short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sound in mind means sane

indicators.note: in a down clue the question word sits over the M

parts.note: how is a question word

explanation.surface: A producer asks how millions are invested in sound that's not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: SANE loses its E to give SAN, which takes in HOW and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A showman is an impresario who stages shows and spectacles.

clue.text: Shy about beginning to practise reproduction

indicators.note: the shy word goes about, around, the letter

parts.note: coy means shy, bashful

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A timid person is starting to rehearse having children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' suggests breeding; it means a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a replica or duplicate of an original.

clue.text: Father with point about American films

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the point word goes about, around, the American letter

parts.note: a tine is a prong, a sharp point

explanation.surface: Dad and a friend argue over American movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' suggests cinema; it is the plural noun for thin coatings.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin surface layer formed by age, like the green coating on bronze.

clue.text: Place never accommodating Welsh on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the result reads backwards
to accommodate is to house, so the Welsh letter goes inside

parts.note: not means in no way, never

explanation.surface: A spot that never welcomes the Welsh, if you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside NOT to give NWOT; that reflected gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a settlement, an inhabited place.

clue.text: Number working to get source of ectoplasm — content of empty room?

parts.note: on means operating, working

indicators.note: a word's source is its first letter

explanation.surface: A medium gets ectoplasm from a vacant, haunted room.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty room holds nobody at all, so its occupants are nobody.

clue.text: I note contest involving league is ongoing?

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so the league letter goes inside

parts.note: to compete is to contest

explanation.surface: A remark that a league competition is still running.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still going on is unfinished, not yet complete.

clue.text: Copper, say, taking time tucking into breakfast, perhaps …

indicators.note: tucking into means pushing inside, so the time letter goes into the meal

parts.note: breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A policeman takes his time over breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an example of a metal, a chemical element.

clue.text: The writer backed inclination to suppress old stupid expression

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, me

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
dim means stupid

explanation.surface: The author supports a tendency to censor outdated foolish language.
explanation.definitionFit: An embodiment is the tangible manifestation of an idea or quality.

clue.text: … breakfast item for one? Good

parts.note: e.g., for example, means 'for one'

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the clue above: a breakfast item is good, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg, boiled or fried, is a standard morning meal food.

clue.text: Square indicated by cube here?

parts.note: this clue is 27-across, and 27 is the cube of 3; the square of 3 is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number is 27, three cubed; squaring the same three gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Three squared gives this number, while three cubed gives the clue's own number.

clue.text: Mean suggestion from some Londoners? The last thing you need

indicators.note: many Londoners drop their aitches, so the word loses its H

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion
the end is the last thing

explanation.surface: Some Londoners propose something unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords assume Cockney Londoners drop the H sound, so HINT becomes 'INT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to mean to do something, to have it as a purpose.

clue.text: Lacerations found around most of vulgar waterproofs

indicators.note: the cuts are found around, so they enclose the shortened word

parts.note: gashes are deep cuts, lacerations

indicators.note: most of the word means dropping its last letter

parts.note: low means coarse, vulgar

explanation.surface: Cuts found around coarse rainwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are rubber overshoes worn to keep feet dry.
